A Snapshot of Your Day

Join Siemens Energy as Head of Primary Engineering and lead and develop our Primary Engineering organization supporting complex high-voltage substation projects, both onshore and offshore. The role combines people leadership, technical leadership, engineering execution and resource management. You will ensure that the team has the competencies, capacity, methods and technical expertise required to deliver safe, compliant and high-quality engineering solutions across our project portfolio. Passionate about developing people and building strong engineering capabilities, you provide clear direction while empowering engineers to take technical ownership and grow professionally. Combining technical understanding with a dedicated approach to quality, risk, cost and schedule, you enjoy working across organizational and technical boundaries to continuously improve how engineering is delivered.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Lead, develop and motivate the Primary Engineering team, strengthening technical competence, ownership and collaboration

• Create clear development paths for engineers and technical specialists through mentoring, challenging project assignments and structured competence development, and attract young engineering talent through relationships with universities and technical institutions, student projects and internships

• Lead the Primary Engineering scope across our projects, including electromechanical verification of the complete primary system and substation system design

• Ensure high-quality engineering of AIS and GIS substations, including SLDs, layouts and sections, electrical clearances, earthing and lightning protection, HV equipment and cable integration and 2D/3D design

• Maintain strong technical governance, ensuring compliance with project requirements, applicable standards and engineering guidelines, and support technical reviews and the resolution of complex engineering challenges across the project portfolio

• Manage engineering resources and competencies across multiple projects and global engineering hubs, identifying capacity and competence gaps and establishing appropriate mitigation

• Drive standardization, digitalization and continuous improvement of engineering methods, tools and workflows, including the adoption of automation and AI-enabled engineering solutions where they create value

• Strengthen collaboration with Technical Project Management, Secondary Engineering, Civil Engineering, BIM, Procurement, suppliers and site execution

What You Bring

• A degree in electrical, mechanical or another relevant engineering discipline

• Extensive experience within HV substation engineering and complex turnkey substations, preferably covering both AIS and GIS technologies and including offshore substations or major grid infrastructure projects

• Strong understanding of substation system design and electromechanical aspects of HV equipment and installations, including equipment integration, electrical clearances, earthing, lightning protection and mechanical interfaces

• Knowledge of relevant HV standards and engineering practices, including IEC 61936 and EN 50522

• Proven experience leading, developing and motivating engineers and technical specialists, combined with strong capabilities in resource planning and prioritization across multiple projects

• A pragmatic leadership style combining technical depth, people development and business understanding

• Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills across projects, customers, suppliers, engineering disciplines and international locations

• Professional fluency in English; Danish is considered an advantage

About the Team

As Head of Primary Engineering, you lead a team of approximately 10 engineers and specialists based in Denmark, supported by colleagues in our global engineering hubs, including Serbia, Croatia and India. The team delivers primary engineering solutions for complex substation projects and works closely with project management, engineering and execution teams across the business.

Our Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Siemens Energy offers a leading portfolio and solutions in HVDC transmission, grid stabilization and storage, high voltage switchgears and transformers, and digital grid technology.

Who is Siemens Energy?

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity, we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

Create engaging video & photo content for Denmark’s favorite maternity brand!

About Momkind

We are a dynamic, fast-growing e-commerce brand based in Copenhagen, and we are looking for a creative, trend-obsessed Social Media & Content Creation Intern to bring our brand to life across our visual channels! At Momkind (momkind.dk), we are building an honest, supportive, and empowering universe for mothers. From our essential postpartum recovery products and comfortable maternity wear to our vibrant online community and blog, we break down taboos surrounding motherhood with authenticity, care, and humor.

What You’ll Do

As our Social Media & Content Creator, you will be at the front lines of our organic social channels (TikTok & Instagram) and digital presence. You’ll work directly with our marketing team to turn creative ideas into scroll-stopping visual content.

• 
Content Creation (Photo & Video): Conceptualize, film, and edit engaging short-form video content (TikToks, Instagram Reels, UGC-style videos) and high-quality photography for our social feeds and e-commerce website.

• 
Diverse Content Styles: Produce everything from aesthetic product showcases and product explainers to humorous, relatable trending videos and authentic behind-the-scenes content from photoshoots, store events, and everyday office life.

• 
Trend Spotting & Execution: Stay on top of audio trends, meme formats, and social media viral moments, quickly pitching and executing relevant ideas tailored to our audience.

• 
Copywriting: Craft fun, engaging captions, on-screen text, and hooks that resonate with our community of mamas and moms-to-be.

• 
Event & Project Support: Assist on-site with photoshoots, store events, and other exciting marketing campaigns.

• 
Performance Curiosity: Collaborate with the team to analyze content performance, testing what works best and continually refining our content strategy based on data.

Who You Are

We are looking for someone who loves social media (especially TikTok), video editing, and isn't afraid to step in front of or behind the camera to produce quick, on-trend content.

• 
Education: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Marketing, Digital Media, Communication, Visual Design, or a related field.

• 
Creative & Bold: You have a strong visual eye, passion for branding, and aren't afraid to try new creative concepts or experiment with funny/trending video ideas on the fly.

• 
SoMe Native: You naturally stay up to date on TikTok and Instagram trends, algorithm shifts, and emerging digital content styles.

• 
Data-Curious: You don't just love creating content—you are genuinely curious about reach, engagement, and understanding why certain videos go viral or drive conversions.

• 
Work Experience: Prior experience in content creation, video editing (CapCut, Premiere, InShot, Canva, etc.), or managing brand social channels is preferred (portfolio or work samples are a huge plus!).

• 
Language: Fluent in English. If you can speak Dutch, Swedish, or German, it is a plus.

What We Offer

• 
Paid Position: Fair compensation.

• 
Real Impact & Creative Freedom: Your ideas won't just sit in a pitch document—you'll see them come to life across channels with thousands of active followers.

• 
Flexibility: Work 8–10 hours a week (2 days in the office) with schedule flexibility designed to fit around your university classes and exams.

• 
Growth & Mentorship: Gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced DTC e-commerce environment, learning directly from experienced e-commerce and brand marketers.

• 
Warm Team Culture: Join an open, supportive, and passionate team located in Copenhagen.

• 
Perks: Free lunch, office located in the city center, and a great discount on momkind products!

How to Apply

Ready to bring your creative energy to momkind?

Please send your CV, a short cover letter, and a link to your portfolio, TikTok/Instagram profile, or video work samples if available.

• Contact Person: Lauren Blair Klarskov

We review applications on a rolling basis, so don't hesitate to reach out! We can't wait to meet you.

For more information or questions please contact us at lauren@momkind.dk

Working at

momkind

Momkind is a Ecommerce business founded in 2019 offering products for pregnancy, postpartum, nursing and beyond. Through co-creation with the momkind community we test and develop products for all stages of motherhood. Working at momkind is fun, engaging and interesting. We work collaboratively, and we dare to take risks and to learn from our mistakes. We're on a growth journey and becoming part of the company in this stage means loads of responsibility and an exciting opportunity to develop and learn.

Job Description

Would you like to work with financial regulation and compliance while contributing to the development of a growing regulatory services business at Netcompany Banking Services?

As a Business Consultant, you will work with compliance and risk management while supporting legal and governance matters for financial institutions. You will combine your regulatory expertise with an analytical and structured approach to help our customers navigate complex regulatory requirements and strengthen their compliance and risk frameworks.

We are currently expanding our regulatory services offering, where you will play an important role in delivering and further developing our services to financial institutions. Our services within the compliance and risk areas cover the regulatory process from monitoring legislation and assessing compliance risks to annual planning, data-supported compliance reviews and regulatory reporting.

We focus on the use of automation and new technologies to develop efficient and scalable regulatory services. Working closely with colleagues across data and technology, you will contribute to high-quality customer deliveries and the continued development of regulatory Services.

Netcompany Banking Services

We deliver various IT solutions and services to banks and savings institutions across Denmark and other Nordic countries. We provide a modern, cloud-based core banking platform serving more than 50 Nordic banks with over 2 million end customers. Our solutions encompass daily banking operations, mobile and internet banking, payments, investment management, risk management, compliance, and open banking.

Responsibilities

As a Business Consultant, you will support the Head of Regulatory Banking Services in delivering high-quality regulatory services to financial institutions. You will contribute to daily customer deliveries while helping to develop and standardise processes, control frameworks and reporting models.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• 
Prepare and maintain compliance risk assessments and annual compliance plans for financial clients.

• 
Develop control frameworks, control questions and supporting documentation, including reviewing and quality-assuring data and control results.

• 
Prepare compliance review reports, quarterly and annual reports, and follow up on identified risks, observations and recommendations.

• 
Monitor and assess relevant financial regulation and contribute to translating regulatory requirements into control activities, policies, procedures and governance documentation.

• 
Contribute to the development of regulatory services, including supporting risk management activities and collaborating with data and technology specialists to improve and automate processes.

About you

We imagine that you have:

• 
A relevant academic degree, such as law, business law or a related field, combined with around 2–5 years of experience in compliance, financial regulation or similar areas.

• 
Solid knowledge of financial regulation and preferably experience from a compliance function within a financial institution, ideally in the second line of defence.

• 
Practical experience with regulatory risk assessments, control frameworks, documentation and compliance reporting. Experience with risk management is an advantage.

• 
Strong analytical and communication skills, a structured approach to your work and an interest in data, technology and the digitalisation of regulatory processes.

• 
Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must. Your day-to-day working environment will, however, primarily be Danish-speaking.

Join an inclusive community

We highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand your network.

Send us an application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

You’ll build and operate production pipelines that our traders rely on daily, learning alongside senior data practitioners and taking on greater ownership as your experience grows.

Here’s what the job entails

You will build, migrate and operate data ingestion pipelines, helping modernise how shared market data reaches our users. Working with senior data modellers and data-quality specialists, you will take responsibility for both the code you deliver and how it runs in production. This gives you hands-on experience of large-scale platform modernisation while developing your engineering skills.

More specifically, your responsibilities include:

• migrating existing data collectors (which fetch market and vendor data from websites, APIs and files) onto our modern data platform via our Python and C# based ingestion framework

• building new pipelines that deliver data both to the lakehouse (Databricks/Delta Lake) and to existing trading data systems

• making pipelines reliable: automated tests, data-quality checks, safe re-runs and the ability to reload historical data

• operating and improving the pipelines you build: monitoring data delivery, investigating failures and fixing recurring problems

• working with data scientists to understand their data requirements and make shared source datasets clean, reproducible and ready for use in forecasting and trading models

• contributing with documented examples and reusable pipeline patterns, helping other teams work with shared data and apply our engineering standards

Meet your team

You will join Data Platform Enablement, the team that makes shared external market data trustworthy, consistent and reusable across Danske Commodities. We build and operate the pipelines that collect and harmonise this data, and establish common engineering methods, modelling principles and quality standards. Working alongside Data Platform Infrastructure, which provides the underlying platform capabilities, we help product teams, analysts and data scientists build on a reliable data foundation.

We are a newly formed team of six experienced data practitioners, growing to eight team members, and our backgrounds are currently within data engineering, data modelling, and data science. We are a hands-on team, where we set standards, but we also build and ship and we invest in growing the people who join us. We always seek to leave systems simpler and better documented than we found them.

But enough about us… over to you!

As you will be owning production pipelines and be expected to drive improvements, we imagine that you enjoy taking responsibility for your work and learning from the knowledge around you. We also picture you as a curious person, who is willing to learn more about the field we work in.

Furthermore, we imagine that you:

• hold a relevant educational background within computer science, software engineering, data science or similar – or equivalent practical experience

• have hands-on experience building data pipelines or data applications in Python, SQL or C#

• have a working knowledge of SQL and relational databases

• are familiar with version control (Git)

• are proficient in English - both written and spoken

Please note that prior knowledge of the energy sector is not required for this role.

We’ll take good care of you

jobs.description:
Landfolk is growing, and we want to make our support across booking channels even better. We’re looking for a Team Manager as a maternity cover for our international Guest & Host Care team, with a particular focus on the external booking channels we work with, including Airbnb, Booking.com, Holidu, HomeToGo and Vrbo.

What excites us about this role

Great support starts with a team that has the confidence, guidance and tools to help. Your day-to-day work will bring together people and operations. You’ll create the conditions for your team to succeed, help your colleagues grow and ensure guests and hosts receive knowledgeable, personal support, with quality at every step.

You’ll work closely with the other Team Managers to set clear priorities, maintain high service standards and build a supportive, motivated team. You’ll also help shape the workflows that make our collaboration with external booking channels work in practice.

You’ll lead by example in support and turn everyday experience, feedback and data into improvements to our processes, tools and collaboration. You’ll have real influence on how we work, in a tech-driven organisation that actively uses data, automation, agents and AI.

What you’ll actually do

You’ll balance daily support, people management and improvements to how the team works.

Your key responsibilities:

• 
Lead and develop your team members through ongoing guidance, monthly one-to-ones and specific, constructive feedback

• 
Ensure helpful, timely support by email, chat and phone, with clear standards for quality and follow-up

• 
Develop support workflows for external booking channels, so the team can confidently navigate both Landfolk’s processes and those of each platform

• 
Help resolve complex guest and host cases, disputes and compensation requests within agreed guidelines

• 
Plan shifts for our student employees and ensure coverage during holidays, sickness and peak season

• 
Take part in recruitment and creating thoughtful onboarding programmes together with your manager and relevant colleagues

• 
Use data and support insights to improve service quality, response times and workflows

• 
Build a supportive, inclusive team culture with room for learning, ownership and honest feedback

The role calls for flexibility and availability to meet the needs of the team and the business, particularly during peak season(s).

About you

You’re motivated by helping both people and operations succeed. You bring structure to a busy day, set clear priorities and stay calm when a situation needs extra care.

You might be a great fit if you:

• 
Have experience in customer service, support, hospitality or a marketplace business, ideally with previous team leadership or people management responsibilities.

• 
Enjoy helping others develop through practical conversations, coaching and feedback.

• 
Can balance high service standards, efficient operations and your team’s well-being.

• 
Take a structured approach to staffing, follow-up and process improvements.

• 
Are comfortable picking up the phone yourself and handling difficult conversations with guests and hosts.

• 
Are curious about our tech-driven organisation and how data, automation and AI can support great service.

• 
Are fluent in written and spoken English. Additional language skills are a plus, but not a requirement.

Experience with external booking platforms is an advantage. What matters most is your ability to learn new systems and turn complex workflows into a straightforward day-to-day experience for the team.

Curious about Landfolk?

At Landfolk, we believe the most memorable holidays happen in homes that are loved and lived in. We’re united by curiosity and driven by a shared purpose of helping people reconnect with nature, culture and the people they love.

Here’s a chance to make your mark on a fast-growing and purpose-driven scaleup with more than 9,000 handpicked holiday homes in Norway, Sweden, Germany, Italy, France, Spain and Denmark.

With us, you’ll:

• 
Learn and grow with more than 100 talented colleagues across tech, commercial, customer care, and creative teams

• 
Be trusted, take ownership and let curiosity guide your work and development

• 
Work in a welcoming, open-minded atmosphere where teamwork and laughs come naturally

• 
Explore how AI can support your work, experiment with your team, and share what you learn

• 
Enjoy flexible working hours, a beautiful office in Aarhus and plenty of moments to come together

• 
Join trips to beautiful holiday homes

Together we’ve already accomplished pretty impressive results, and we’re nowhere near done. Read more about Landfolk

Ready to join us?

Your CV doesn’t have to tick every box. We’re interested in how you think, the questions you ask, and the ideas you’re excited to explore.

Send us your CV and a few words about why you’d like to join the team. Include your answers in a short cover letter and send it along with your CV.

We review applications and interview candidates on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as you’re ready, and no later than 30 November 2026.

Interested?

**Would you like to use your PCB design skills to create advanced hearing devices that help people with hearing loss connect more easily with the world around them?

**As a PCB Designer at GN Hearing, you will follow your designs from early ideas and prototypes through to finished products ready for production.

Whether you bring established PCB design experience or are ready to build further on a solid foundation, you will have knowledgeable colleagues around you and opportunities to contribute your perspective.

**Welcome to GN Hearing

**You will join Electronic Integration, part of Product Development in R&D at our headquarters in Ballerup. We are responsible for making the electronic components in our hearing aids as compact as possible while maintaining reliable performance and signal integrity.

We work closely with colleagues in mechanical design, electroacoustics, software, radio systems and production. Our team values practical problem-solving and knowledge-sharing, with room for questions and learning from different levels of experience.

**Your contribution is appreciated, and you will:

**

• Design schematics and PCB layouts in Cadence Allegro and OrCAD Capture

• Contribute to PCB solutions from concept development and prototyping through to production release

• Review solutions and design test verification together with PCB design colleagues to resolve issues early

• Work with cross-functional project teams to inform design decisions and develop new solutions

• Collaborate with our production unit in Præstø to make sure that designs are manufacturable

• Create clear and accurate PCB documentation

• Participate in sourcing and qualifying PCB suppliers

**To perform well in the role, we imagine that you:

**

• Bring a relevant degree, e.g. a bachelor’s in electronic engineering

• Have experience with PCB design, and would like to continue developing your skills in a product development environment

• May have experience with PCB manufacturing, assembly processes and IPC standards

• Are familiar with PCB design tools such as Cadence Allegro, OrCAD Capture or Capture CIS Database, or are willing to learn relevant tools

• Enjoy working closely with others to create quality outcomes

• Can communicate proficiently in English

We pride ourselves on encouraging flexible work whenever possible. We trust our people to fulfill their responsibilities, to know when in-person collaboration is better than hybrid, and to be present when it is needed most.

**We are focused on an inclusive recruitment process

**All applicants will receive equal consideration for employment. As such, we encourage you to submit your CV without a photo to ensure an equal and fair application process.

Should you have any special requirements for the interview, please let the Hiring Manager know upon accepting the invitation to the interview.

**How to apply?

**Use the ‘APPLY’ link no later than November 27, 2026. Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, and we may close the position before the application deadline if we find the right candidate. We therefore encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Feel free to only submit your up-to-date CV, including a few sentences outlining your motivation for applying.

**Join us in bringing people closer

**GN brings people closer through our advanced intelligent hearing, audio, video, and gaming solutions. Inspired by people and motivated by innovation, we deliver technology that enhances the senses of hearing and sight. We enable people with hearing loss to overcome real-life problems, improve communication and collaboration for businesses, and provide great experiences for audio and gaming users.

GN Store Nord A/S has entered into a definitive agreement for the sale of GN’s Hearing business to Amplifon S.p.A. to create a global leader in audiology. For GN Group, this creates an opportunity to expand our position in the large audio and video peripherals markets. Read more about the announcement **here.

****We hope you will join us on this journey and look forward to receiving your application.

**

**WHY SPEKTR

**At spektr, we are on a mission to automate the world’s most complex compliance workflows through AI. Founded by the team behind HelloFlow (acquired by Trulioo), spektr is building the infrastructure and AI agents to run compliance at scale.

_Compliance, built like product.

_Financial services has changed enormously. Much of the technology behind compliance hasn’t. Teams still spend hours on manual checks, disconnected systems slow down launches, and entering a new market can mean rebuilding the same processes all over again.

Are you an experienced software engineer looking for something different? Imagine developing software in the morning, testing it on real hardware in the afternoon, and eventually watching it take flight.

At Acodyne, you will work alongside engineers developing next-generation unmanned aircraft, applying your software engineering experience to challenges that extend far beyond the screen.

You will have the opportunity to work across the software stack, from embedded systems and flight control integration to simulation, telemetry, and ground-based applications. You'll join a small, ambitious team where your contributions will have a direct impact on the aircraft we build.

Your Role

As part of our growing engineering team, you will develop and integrate software for our high-speed, heavy-lift cargo UAVs and their supporting systems.

You will work closely with electronics, mechanical, and aerospace engineers to turn ideas into working solutions, taking software from development through simulation, hardware integration, and real-world flight testing.

We believe that reliable software starts with good engineering practices. Code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and reproducible builds are important parts of how we want to develop our systems.

You will:

• 
Develop and maintain software for our aircraft and supporting systems.

• 
Work with embedded Linux platforms, flight computers, sensors, actuators, and communication systems.

• 
Integrate and extend existing flight control technologies such as ArduPilot or PX4.

• 
Develop tools for telemetry collection, monitoring, data analysis, and ground control.

• 
Build and maintain simulation environments and automated tests to validate software before flight.

• 
Contribute to reliable development workflows, continuous integration, testing, and release processes.

• 
Collaborate across engineering disciplines to integrate and troubleshoot software and hardware.

• 
Participate in prototype development, system integration, and flight test activities.

• 
Document software designs, interfaces, and test results to support future certification and compliance.

About You

We're looking for an experienced software engineer who enjoys solving challenging technical problems and takes pride in building reliable, maintainable software.

You've worked in a professional software development environment and understand the value of good engineering practices. Version control, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and reproducible builds are a natural part of how you work.

You're comfortable taking ownership, making pragmatic engineering decisions, and collaborating with people from different technical backgrounds. You enjoy learning new technologies and aren't afraid to venture beyond your existing expertise.

You don't need to be an aerospace expert. We value strong software engineering fundamentals, technical curiosity, and the ability to master new domains.

You likely have:

• 
Several years of professional software development experience.

• 
Strong programming skills in C/C++ and experience developing software for Linux.

• 
Experience working with modern development workflows, including Git, code reviews, automated testing, and CI/CD.

• 
An understanding of software architecture, debugging, and maintaining complex software systems.

• 
Some experience with embedded systems, hardware interfaces, or resource-constrained environments.

• 
A pragmatic, hands-on approach to engineering and an interest in working with physical systems.

• 
The ability to work independently while contributing constructively to a multidisciplinary team.

It would be a plus if you have:

• 
Experience with robotics, UAVs, autonomous systems, or flight control software.

• 
Familiarity with ArduPilot, PX4, MAVLink, or similar technologies.

• 
Experience with simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or real-time systems.

• 
Knowledge of networking, telemetry, data acquisition, or distributed systems.

• 
Experience using AI-assisted development tools or working with machine learning technologies.

We don't expect you to tick every box. We're more interested in your engineering mindset, technical curiosity, and ability to learn.

As an early-stage startup pushing the boundaries of innovation, we offer a salary typical for our phase of growth.

Acodyne is on a mission to develop the world's fastest unmanned eVTOL aircraft for heavy payloads, initially to serve off-shore, remote areas and general logistics.

**Apylon is building agents for the most complex workflow out there - financial admin in healthcare.

Hospitals and payers move billions of euros through fragmented, manual workflows shaped by clinical data, payer rules, contracts, and local coding systems. We believe this is a data, machine-learning, and automation problem disguised as financial operations.

We are live with leading private hospitals and expanding quickly. Every hospital presents a different challenge: EHR systems are configured differently, national coding rules vary, and contracts describe the same clinical event in different terms. Your job is to help us turn that complexity into a system that learns: each new integration should make the next one faster, safer, and less expensive.

Apylon is backed by experienced operators and top-tier investors in healthcare and fintech. Our team draws on experience from Zendesk, Pleo, Wawa Fertility, Sibill, and some of the largest multi-country hospital groups in Europe. You’ll join the first small engineering team, with massive ownership over both what we build and how we build it.

Delivering healthcare is hard. Getting paid for it shouldn’t be.

You’ll be responsible for

• Own EHR integrations end to end: APIs, schemas, undocumented behaviour, operational failure modes, and vendor changes.

• Build reusable integration-platform primitives for extraction, normalisation, versioning, replay, monitoring, and observability.

• Design the canonical data model that connects heterogeneous EHR data, reimbursement systems, national coding standards, and hospital-specific conventions.

• Build reliable inputs for our billing agents, including the constraints, validation, and evaluation systems that make model-assisted decisions safe to use in production.

• Work directly with hospital IT teams and EHR vendors: technical discovery, implementation, joint debugging, and onboarding.

• Take responsibility for the full lifecycle of your work: design, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and iteration from real-world data.

Who you are

• Experience using LLMs as production components—not just developer tools. You understand when to use models, when deterministic systems are better, how to constrain outputs, and how to evaluate reliability.

• Strong data-modelling instincts. You know when abstraction creates leverage and when it hides important real-world variation.

• Confidence in customer-facing technical work: discovery calls, debugging sessions, and direct conversations with vendors and hospital IT teams.

• Experience with cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.

• A practical, hands-on approach: equally comfortable designing an integration architecture and writing a quick script to answer an urgent question.

This role may be a strong fit if

You enjoy reverse-engineering systems you do not control, finding structure in messy real-world data, and turning one-off discoveries into reusable software. You are comfortable being the engineer in the room with customers and partners.

What this role is not

• Consulting or bespoke delivery work. Each integration must improve the product and reduce the marginal cost of the next.

• A role insulated from customers or operational reality.

• Pure platform engineering or pure integration work: the value comes from doing both.

• A role where incorrect mappings are merely technical defects. In this domain, they can produce incorrect invoices.

Bonus points

• Experience with healthcare interoperability or coding standards, including HL7v2, FHIR, or national messaging and reimbursement standards.

• Experience building and operating third-party integrations at scale.

• Experience in healthcare, fintech, or another regulated environment.

• Experience in an early-stage or fast-growing company.

• Working proficiency in Danish, or German.

Our tech stack

• Python

• Django

• React

• PostgreSQL

• AWS

• K8s

• Terraform

• Bedrock

• We’re pragmatic. You’ll have a big say in how it evolves.

What Apylon offers

• The chance to solve one of Europe’s biggest healthcare inefficiencies.

• Competitive salary + stock options (you’ll own part of what you build).

• 25 days of annual leave + local public holidays.

• Lunch on us during workdays at the office.

If travelling to a hospital basement to figure out why an export is malformed sounds like a bad week, this isn’t your role.

Working at Apylon means embarking on a highly ambitious mission to rebuild the financial infrastructure of European healthcare. We’re already live with leading private hospitals, processing thousands of invoices, proving that complex payer rules can be turned into code, powering transparent, automated, and intelligent revenue systems.

PhD Project in Muscular signaling and metabolism

  Nutrition Exercise and Sports (NEXS), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  The August Krogh Section for Human and Molecular Physiology at Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in “Elucidating the role of AMPK in Skeletal Muscular signaling and metabolism”. The project is part of the research project “Illuminating the signaling architecture of skeletal muscle insulin resistance”, which is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation

  Start date is (expected to be) 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project

  By the use of phophosproteomics in human skeletal muscle, we recently discovered a novel phosphorylation site on AMPK alpha2 subunit regulated by mTORC1. This phosphorylation is associate with glucose uptake. We now wish to explore the relationship between the catabolic signal from AMPK and the anabolic signal from mTORC1 and the potential causal link to metabolic regulation. The project will primarily be conducted in mice by the use of transgenic KI models.

  Who are we looking for?

  We welcome applications from candidates with a strong academic background in physiology, biology, biomedical sciences, exercise science or a related field, and an interest in skeletal muscle physiology and metabolic regulation.

  The project combines animal studies with molecular and metabolic analyses. Experience in one or more relevant areas is an advantage, but applicants are not expected to have all of the skills already. Relevant experience could include in vivo or ex vivo research, metabolic phenotyping, muscle physiology, tissue processing, immunoblotting, immunoprecipitation or tracer-based assays.

  An interest in molecular signalling pathways involved in metabolism, including AMPK and nutrient sensing, would be valuable. Above all, we are looking for a curious and motivated researcher who is keen to learn and develop within a collaborative research environment.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?

  The group is a part of Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports at the Faculty of Scince, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and animal facilities.

  Our group work focuses on the molecular mechanisms through which physical activity promotes metabolic health.

  We are particularly interested in the intracellular interactions between exercise-induced signaling events and those triggered by insulin, aiming to unravel how a single bout of exercise can enhance muscle insulin sensitivity. Central to these studies is the role of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and its interacting partners, including mTOR and TBC1D4.

  We are studying this in humans using various cell/animal models for validation and mechanistic analyses.

  Principal supervisor is Professor Jørgen Wojtaszewski (NEXS, JW@nexs.ku.dk, 45 28751625) and Associate professor Rasmus Kjøbsted (NEXS, Rasmus.Kjobsted@nexs.ku.dk, 45 28344370)

 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.
